verdict: AI memory and HPC catalysts stacking: HIVE BUZZ +25% on $220M sovereign GPU deal, MU +5.5% on Anthropic supply pact ahead of June 24 earnings, ALAB +11% on Nasdaq-100 inclusion; DRAM memflation and HBM 2027 pricing trajectory remain firmly bullish.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (last 24-72h)

**HIVE Digital (BUZZ) — $220M sovereign AI GPU contract** (June 22): HIVE's BUZZ HPC subsidiary closed a USD $220M, 3-year contract with Bell AI Fabric to power Cohere Inc.'s Canadian sovereign AI platform using 2,304 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GB200 NVL72 rack-scale systems at Bell's Merritt, BC facility. Expected ~$70M ARR once operational (late 2026/early 2027), lifting contracted HPC ARR above $100M. B. Riley, Cantor Fitzgerald, Rosenblatt, and Keefe Bruyette all raised price targets. **HIVE +25% (June 22)**. Week's single largest watchlist catalyst.

**Micron (MU) — Anthropic strategic deal** (June 22): Micron announced a multi-year memory/storage supply agreement with Anthropic plus co-design on HBM/DRAM/SSD architecture for AI training and inference; Micron also participated in Anthropic's Series H (~$965B valuation post-money). **MU +~5.5%**. Q3 FY2026 earnings due **June 24**; consensus EPS $20.25 (+942% YoY); sell-side unanimously bullish, HBM sold-out as key backing.

**ALAB (Astera Labs) — Nasdaq-100 inclusion** (effective June 22): ALAB added to NDX, forcing passive QQQ buying. **+11.3% June 21**, +13.5% weekly. Record Q1 revenue $308.4M. Valuation now 39x forward sales and above every Street price target — post-inclusion sell-the-news risk flagged by analysts.

**TrendForce (June 2)** — HBM contract prices expected to surge "multiples higher" in 2027 as buyer-supplier negotiations pivot to HBM4 supply agreements. Tight DRAM supply reinforces supplier pricing power. Baseline correction-risk thesis remains valid but deferred: 2026 pricing intact, risk shifts toward 2028+.

**SK Hynix HBM4 ramp slips Q2 → Q3 2026**: Minor schedule delay flagged (TechPowerUp). Samsung on track for 250K wafers/month by year-end; Micron HBM4 high-yield ramp on 1-beta node proceeding in Q2. 2026 supply still fully sold out.

**Section 232 polysilicon tariff** — Clarification expected by end of June 2026 (PV-Tech). FSLR's CdTe technology is insulated from silicon-chain tariffs and stands to benefit. Silicon-based peers face input-cost uncertainty.

## Context vs Baseline

- **DRAM pricing**: Q1 actuals +93-98% QoQ (vs baseline +90-95% estimate) — slight upside. Q2 guided +58-63% QoQ — rate decelerating but absolute prices surging. Memflation intact.
- **HBM 2027**: TrendForce now calls 2027 HBM prices "multiples higher" as HBM4 negotiation leverage shifts to suppliers. Baseline correction-risk signal looks premature — risk window extends beyond 2027.
- **Hyperscaler capex**: $725B combined 2026 (AMZN $200B, GOOG $175-185B, META $115-135B, MSFT $110-120B). No guide-downs. Baseline intact.
- **Optical**: InP scarcity and COHR/LITE CPO ramp structure unchanged; no fresh 72h news.
- **Solar**: Section 232 polysilicon tariff is the live near-term catalyst; FSLR best positioned.

## Most Important Development

**HIVE BUZZ HPC +25%** on the $220M Bell-Cohere sovereign AI GPU contract (June 22) is the clearest watchlist catalyst — tangible GPU compute contract win plus ARR inflection for a name explicitly flagged for this event type. Close second: **MU-Anthropic strategic partnership** (June 22) anchors direct AI-lab supply ahead of MU's pivotal June 24 earnings, where $20.25 EPS consensus implies +942% YoY growth and HBM sold-out capacity provides beat/raise setup.
